newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Jan 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK Newspaper Headlines - Jan 16.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- MING PAO -- Governor Chris Patten praised the head of the Civil Service, Lam Woon-kwong, and said that former director of immigration Laurence Leung's behaviour had fallen well below the standards of conduct and integrity.
-- A legal service company owned by China might be prosecuted for having operated in the territory for 10 years without registering with the Law Society.

-- ECONOMIC TIMES -- The government recently set up a cross-department team, including officials and representatives from the business sector, to study relations between the government and the business sector. It was led by Financial Secretary Donald Tsang.
-- TA KUNG PAO -- Chinese President Jiang Zemin urged enterprises to accelerate reforms and make proper arrangements for laid-off workers.
-- By 2010, Beijing would present more than 20 sites to the United Nations to be listed in the world cultural heritage index, including the Temple of Heaven and the Summer Palace.

-- APPLE DAILY -- New evidence showed that another pro-Beijing figure, Tsui Tsim-tong, was involved in business dealings with former immigration head Laurence Leung. They were both shareholders of the New China Hong Kong Advertising Ltd.

-- Chinese leader Deng Xiaoping's second son Deng Zhifang was planning to sell his communications company for 150 million yuan. Some analysts believed that the move was a sign of the Deng family's retreat from business.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- Hong Kong was a leading contender to be the International Monetary Fund's Asian headquarters, a move that would boost the territory's claim that it was the region's prominent financial centre. -- China's central bank was ordering state banks to reduce their stakes in domestic debt markets and use the surplus funds to help bolster state enterprises.
-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- The Hong Kong Futures Exchange was studying plans to introduce regional stock futures and expected to launch them early next year.
